techniques.name: Keith Richards Suspended Acoustic Embellishments
techniques.description: Dynamic acoustic fingerpicking and strumming decorated with 2nd-fret hammer-ons and suspended 4th ornamentations (`Am - Asus4`, `E7 - E7sus4`), accompanied by percussive hand mutes

sequence: Pinch open 5th string and 2nd string on beat 1 for Am
Hammer pinky onto 2nd string 3rd fret for the Asus4 suspension
Shift to E7 and hammer 2nd finger onto 3rd string 2nd fret for E7sus4
Strum smoothly through G, F, and resolve to open C
tips: Keep the tempo measured at 72 BPM to let Keith's acoustic flourishes breathe
Use light palm muting between phrases for rhythmic texture
Fmaj7 (X-X-3-2-1-0) can be substituted for F if transitioning quickly

techniques.name: Harmonic Minor Voice Leading & Descending Bass Lines
techniques.description: Navigating the poignant harmonic minor shifts and stepwise bass descent from C down through F to G, emphasizing the G# leading tone in E7 that pulls into the A minor tonic

notes: Harmonic minor leading tone: G# (fret 1 G string in open E7) resolving to A (fret 2 G string in Am)
Stepwise bassline: C (fret 3 A string) to B (fret 2 A string in G/B) to A (open A string in Am)
Borrowed modal submediant: F major (1-3-3-2-1-1) providing romantic sadness
sequence: Highlight the G# note in the E7 chord with an expressive downstroke
Walk the bass cleanly between chord changes to connect the verses
Release the pinky on Asus4 smoothly back into standard Am
Decelerate gently into the final C major resolution
tips: Keep your fretting hand relaxed so acoustic chord changes never stumble
Use a combination of pick and bare fingers (hybrid picking) for softer chord arpeggiations
Listen to Mick Taylor's delicate acoustic counterpoint on the studio master

beginner.title: Master the Open Chords

Strum through the verse progression at 72 BPM
Sing along with the famous chorus hook

intermediate.title: Master Keith Richards' Embellishments
steps: Practice the pinky hammer-on on the 2nd string (Am to Asus4)
Work on the E7sus4 hammer-on on the 3rd string

advanced.title: Complete Solo Acoustic Performance
steps: Combine bass notes, strumming, and melody fills into a continuous flow
Capture the emotional drama of the original Rolling Stones recording
Perform the full ballad with authentic rock ballad presence

commonMistakes: Rushing the 72 BPM tempo — this ballad needs patient spacing and breathing room
Muting the high open E string when fretting the Asus4 pinky hammer-on
Stumbling during the quick shift from F to C in the verse
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Isolated Asus4 and E7sus4 hammer-on drill
5 minutes: Intro arpeggio picking pattern at 72 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus chord transitions (C → G → Dm → Am)
focusAreas: Dynamic separation between verse intimacy and chorus swell
metronomeWork: Practice at 60 BPM with metronome clicks on all four beats
Advance to 72 BPM once intro embellishments are clean and fluid
Set metronome on beats 2 and 4 to develop natural acoustic sway
